facts.statement: Xuanhuaceratops lived during the Late Jurassic Period, specifically the Tithonian stage between 150.8 and 145.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: The genus was in 2006 dated to the Tithonian, 150.8-145.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The dinosaur lived in Asia during the Late Jurassic, spanning approximately from 150 to 145 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 150 y 145 millones de años, desde el Kimmeridgiense al Titoniense

facts.statement: Fossils of Xuanhuaceratops were discovered in the Houcheng Formation in Hebei Province, northeastern China.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in the Houcheng Formation of Hebei Province, northeastern China.

facts.statement: The first fossil specimen was a fragmentary skeleton found in the 1970s by Nie Rongzhen near Yanjiagou.
facts.quote: The first of these was a single, fragmentary skeleton discovered in the 1970s by Nie Rongzhen, near Yanjiagou.

facts.statement: The genus name Xuanhuaceratops means "Xuanhua horned face," combining the Xuanhan region name with Greek words for horn and face.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to the Xuanhan region with Greek keras, "horn", and ops, "face".

facts.statement: The species name 'niei' honors Nie Rongzhen, who donated the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Nie, who donated the holotype, as discoverer.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, IVPP 12722, consists of a partial skeleton that includes a skull.
facts.quote: The holotype IVPP 12722 consists of a partial skeleton with skull.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the holotype specimen was likely a fully grown adult.
facts.quote: The holotype was probably a fully grown individual.

facts.statement: In 2006, the estimated total body length of Xuanhuaceratops was one meter.
facts.quote: In 2006, the total body length of Xuanhuaceratops was estimated at one metre.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of Xuanhuaceratops at six kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight at six kilogrammes.

facts.statement: The animal was considered facultatively bipedal due to its slender upper arm bones, which were only four centimeters long, and its bowed thighbone.
facts.quote: The animal was seen as facultatively bipedal in view of its slender upper arm bones, just four centimetres long, and bowed thighbone.

facts.statement: A distinguishing feature of Xuanhuaceratops is that its premaxilla bears only a single tooth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla bears only a single tooth.

facts.statement: The outer wall of the dentary bone is thickened and covered with a pattern of anastomosing grooves and ridges.
facts.quote: The outer wall of the dentary is thickened and covered by a pattern of anastomosing grooves and ridges.

facts.statement: Xuanhuaceratops belongs to the family Chaoyangsauridae and is considered one of the earliest ceratopsians.
facts.quote: A member of the family Chaoyangsauridae, it was one of the earliest ceratopsians.

facts.statement: In 2006, Xuanhuaceratops was classified within Chaoyangsauridae, a lineage of Ceratopsia that is basal to all neoceratopsians and psittacosaurids.
facts.quote: Xuanhuaceratops niei was in 2006 placed in the Chaoyangsauridae, a clade in phylogenetic analyses recovered as a lineage of Ceratopsia basal to all neoceratopsians and psittacosaurids.

facts.statement: The name Xuanhuasaurus niei was originally published in 1985 but was invalid because it lacked a description and a specified holotype.
facts.quote: The species name Xuanhuasaurus niei was published by Zhao Xijin in a 1985 study, but without a description (or even a specified holotype) making it an invalid nomen nudum.

facts.statement: Three additional fossil specimens were discovered in the summer of 2003.
facts.quote: In the summer of 2003, fossil fragments from three additional specimens were discovered.

facts.statement: In 2006, Xuanhuaceratops niei was classified within Chaoyangsauridae, a clade identified as a basal lineage of Ceratopsia for all neoceratopsians and psittacosaurids.
facts.quote: Xuanhuaceratops niei fue colocado en 2006 en Chaoyangsauridae, un clado en análisis filogenéticos recuperado como un linaje de Ceratopsia basal para todos los neoceratopsianos y psitacosáuridos.

facts.statement: Later research demonstrated that Dianchungosaurus was actually a crocodylomorph, not a dinosaur.
facts.quote: más tarde se demostró que Dianchungosaurus era un crocodilomorfo.

facts.statement: Xuanhuaceratops lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Valanginian stages, between 152.21 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Valanginian (152.21 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Xuanhuaceratops belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The genus Xuanhuaceratops was named by Zhao and colleagues in 2006.
facts.quote: Zhao et al. 2006

rejected.statement: The species Xuanhuaceratops niei was formally named in 2006 by Zhao Xijin, Cheng Zhengwu, Xu Xing, and Peter J. Makovicky in the journal Acta Geologica Sinica.
rejected.quote: The type species Xuanhuaceratops niei was named in the journal Acta Geologica Sinica by Zhao Xijin, Cheng Zhengwu, Xu Xing, and Peter J. Makovicky.

rejected.statement: The Chaoyangsauridae family was initially considered invalid because it lacked a validly named type genus.
rejected.quote: Esta familia no era válida debido a que carecía de un género de tipo con nombre válido.
